records.name: Philadelphia Medical Reserve Corps
records.summary: A city-run volunteer unit of more than 5,000 people, medical and non-medical, that helps during health emergencies, disasters, and big public events.
records.what_you_do: Members can be sent to emergencies or large events such as marathons, and are asked to take part in at least one practice session, exercise, or deployment each year. Every applicant has a background check.

schedule.text: Volunteers are sent out when the city needs help, during emergencies and big events. After acceptance, new members attend an orientation, in person or by video.

first_step.how: Register online through the state site linked from the city page, or email mrc@phila.gov, or call (215) 629-6634 to ask about the next orientation
first_step.basis: Open to any adult 18 or older with a clear way to sign up, and medical training is not required.

records.notes: The city page shows no date. The sign of life comes from the April 2025 city article, which says volunteers worked at the city's warming centers in January 2025.

records.name: Second Alarmers Association of Philadelphia
records.summary: A volunteer association that brings meals, warm supplies, and rest support to first responders at fires, police incidents, and big city events.
records.what_you_do: Members give about 20 hours a month through on-scene calls, standby details, and work at the station, and attend 8 of the 12 monthly meetings each year. Applicants must be 18 or older, hold a Pennsylvania or New Jersey driver's license, have a high school diploma or GED, and be able to lift 20 to 50 pounds regularly.

schedule.text: Association meetings are held on the first Monday of each month at 8 pm, moved to the next Monday when that day is a holiday. The station lists 24/7 operating hours.

first_step.how: Fill out the membership application online or as a PDF, submit it, and sit for an interview. Accepted applicants are voted on at an association meeting and then start as probationary members for 12 months.
first_step.basis: An application, an interview, and a member vote come before you see the work, so the way in is not open to casual visitors.

records.notes: The group's site shows a 2023 copyright, which was not used as evidence. The sign of life is the April 2025 city article (meals for first responders at the February 2025 Eagles parade). Membership is by application and vote, so open_to is public with a newcomer score of 2.

records.name: Team Rubicon
records.summary: A national disaster response group whose volunteers, called Greyshirts, deploy after disasters and do home repair and recovery work. Its volunteers helped finish flood repairs in Philadelphia's Eastwick neighborhood in November 2024.
records.what_you_do: After signing up, pass a background check, finish the first training mission, and then accept deployment invitations when a response needs volunteers. Work areas include disaster response, long-term recovery, medical support, and workforce development.

schedule.text: No set hours. Volunteers deploy when an operation needs them, and the group asks for as much time as each person can give.

first_step.how: Register on the Roll Call system with your email, phone, and street address, describe your skills and interests, pass the background check, and complete the TR101 first training mission
first_step.basis: Anyone can sign up online, but the background check and first training come before any deployment.

records.notes: National group. Its volunteer page names no Philadelphia team or chapter. The Philadelphia work comes from the city's April 2025 article. The page does not state an age limit, so min_age is left out.

records.name: Pennsylvania Animal Response Team
records.summary: A statewide nonprofit of volunteers who help animals and the people who care for them during disasters and emergencies, such as house fires and loose livestock. The City of Philadelphia points local volunteers to its Philadelphia County division.
records.what_you_do: After basic training, volunteers answer calls for animal help: delivering pet care kits to families displaced by house fires, moving loose farm animals, trapping cats for rescue groups, and helping an animal that is down.

schedule.text: Response is on call when animals need help, anywhere in Pennsylvania. Training courses and public training sessions are listed on the group's site.

first_step.how: Sign up on the group's volunteer sign-up page, then take the basic training for CART membership. The site's contact form can help you choose a course.
first_step.basis: Public sign-up and public training sessions are listed, though the page sets no eligibility rules beyond signing up and training.

records.notes: The city page names a Philadelphia County Animal Response division, but the group's site, read on 2026-10-08, names no Philadelphia division, so the local link is not confirmed. The activity log on the home page runs from September 2 to October 4, 2026. The email address is hidden on the page, so the contact form at https://paanimalresponse.org/contact/ is listed in notes only.

records.name: The Salvation Army, Greater Philadelphia
records.summary: A faith-based charity whose Greater Philadelphia unit uses volunteers for meals, holiday service, and disaster response. In February 2025, its volunteers served meals to first responders during the plane crash recovery and at the Eagles parade.
records.what_you_do: Serve meals, help with facilities, ring bells during the holidays, work with youth, or join disaster response when it is needed. Start from the local volunteer page to pick a role.

schedule.text: Some roles are one-time, such as holiday bell ringing, and others are ongoing. The page says locations need volunteers throughout the year, with no set dates listed.

first_step.how: Choose a role on the Greater Philadelphia volunteer page and sign up there. For disaster response, use the national Salvation Army disaster volunteer sign-up form linked from that page.
first_step.basis: Open to the public through a published sign-up, though the page lists no training or start date.

records.notes: The volunteer page does not describe disaster roles or training and gives no dates. The national disaster sign-up form at disaster.salvationarmyusa.org was linked but not opened. The city article is the source for the 2025 meal work.

records.name: American Red Cross, Southeastern Pennsylvania
records.summary: The Red Cross regional office for southeastern Pennsylvania uses volunteers to staff city evacuation shelters and reunification sites and to help people after home fires.
records.what_you_do: Volunteers staff the city's evacuation shelters when they open, work reunification sites at large events, and help people displaced by home fires.

schedule.text: Shifts depend on need: the city's evacuation shelters, large events that need a reunification site, and home fires.

records.notes: Every Red Cross page checked returned HTTP 403, so sign-up steps, training, and volunteer roles are not recorded. All facts come from the city's April 2025 article. Needs a check from a browser before the record is trusted. A search result mentioned a Red Cross amateur radio volunteer team, which was not verified and is not recorded.

records.name: Southeastern Pennsylvania VOAD
records.summary: A coalition of disaster relief groups in the Philadelphia region that plans together before disasters and matches community needs with member services afterward.
records.what_you_do: Member groups train and plan together and share resources during response and recovery. The coalition also offers free disaster training to community and business groups.

first_step.how: Most people reach the coalition through one of its member groups. Community groups that want to help in emergencies can email the city's Office of Emergency Management at oem@phila.gov.
first_step.basis: The coalition's own pages could not be read, so how a single person can join is not confirmed.

records.notes: The coalition's own site returned HTTP 404 on two checks, and sepavoad.org did not resolve, so its member list was not read. The city article credits members with the July 2024 Rhawnhurst fire response and the November 2024 Eastwick repairs. The coalition is for organizations, so open_to is members.

leads_only.note: A search pointed to a university amateur radio club's meeting notes that mention a Philadelphia County ARES group. The PDF could not be read as text, so no facts were recorded. Confirm through the ARRL section emergency coordinator.

leads_only.note: Named in a June 2013 news article about a Field Day exercise. No current evidence and no own website found, so probably dormant. Not recorded.

leads_only.note: A search result named it as a Temple campus radio club. The event page now redirects to Temple's home page, and no club website was found. Not checked further.

leads_only.name: Red Paw Emergency Relief Team
leads_only.note: Named in the city's April 2025 volunteer week article as the group of a volunteer leader at an evacuation shelter. No website or contact is given there.

leads_only.name: Eastwick unmet needs group
leads_only.note: Per the city's April 2025 article, a group backed by local faith and community organizations that finished the last Eastwick home repairs after the 2020 flood. No name, website, or contact is given.
